# MCP tool reference

<!-- Generated by docs/generate-mcp-reference.py from the running server; do not edit by hand. -->

OpenJersey offers 34 tools over [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io). See [Working with AI assistants](ai-assistants.md) for how to connect a client and what a session looks like.

Positions are millimetres on the print sheet (x right, y down) unless a garment position is given: `panel` (`front` or `back`), `across_mm` (from the centre line, positive towards the wearer's left) and `above_hem_mm`. Colours are `#rrggbb`.

## Look at the design

### `get_overview`

Sheet size, every garment piece with its position and size in mm, the garment coordinate convention, base colours and a short object summary.

*read-only*

### `list_objects`

The object tree (top of the stack first) with id, name, type, position (mm), rotation, scale, size (mm), visibility and kind-specific fields.

*read-only*

### `get_object`

One object by id, with its kind-specific fields (and children for groups).

*read-only*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | integer | required |

### `list_garments`

The garment library: id, name, kind (top | bottom), body and whether it is unisex. Filter by kind and/or body. Use the id with set_garment.

*read-only*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `man` \| `women` |  |
| `kind` | `top` \| `bottom` |  |

### `list_presets`

Names of the ready-made designs load_preset accepts.

*read-only*

### `render_preview`

PNG previews: the print sheet and/or the garment from front and back. view = sheet | garment | both (default both). With `piece` (an id from get_overview) the sheet preview is cropped to that piece, to check details.

*read-only*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `piece` | string |  |
| `view` | `sheet` \| `garment` \| `both` |  |

## Colours and garments

### `set_piece_color`

Set a base colour: target = primary | accent | trim (roles) or a region: a piece id from get_overview (front, back, side_l, side_r, sleeve_l, sleeve_r, collar, armhole_l, armhole_r, leg_l, leg_r — depending on the model), cuff_l, cuff_r, leg_stripe_l, leg_stripe_r, leg_hem_l, leg_hem_r.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `color` | string | required · #rrggbb |
| `target` | string | required |

### `set_garments`

Choose which garments the design includes and the plain colour of their inside on the model. A left-out garment is hidden on the model and left off the print sheet (e.g. a warm-up shirt without shorts).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `inside_color` | string | #rrggbb |
| `shirt` | boolean |  |
| `shorts` | boolean |  |

### `set_garment`

Put the design on another top or bottom from the library (get_overview lists them by id), or switch the body (man / women: tops and bottoms follow to the same products where they exist). Objects keep their place on the body; objects on pieces the new garment lacks (e.g. sleeves on a tank top) are hidden.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `body` | `man` \| `women` |  |
| `garment` | `tshirt-man` \| `tshirt-women` \| `sleeveless-shirt-man` \| `sleeveless-shirt-women` \| `longsleeve-shirt-man` \| `longsleeve-shirt-women` \| `game-shorts-man` \| `game-shorts-f5-women` \| `performance-shorts-man` \| `back-panel-shorts-man` \| `fitted-shorts-women` \| `raglan-tshirt-man` \| `raglan-tshirt-women` \| `polo-shirt-man` … |  |

### `load_preset`

Replace the design with a preset for the current model: 'example'.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | required |

## Files

### `new_design`

Start an empty design on the current garments (the previous one stays available through undo).

### `open_design`

Open a saved .json design, replacing the current one (undo brings the previous one back).

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required |

### `save_design`

Save the design as an OpenJersey .json file. Without `path`, saves to the file it was opened from or last saved to.

*can delete or overwrite*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string |  |

### `export_print_template`

Write the print sheet (placeholders left out) as a PNG file for the printer.

*can delete or overwrite*

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `path` | string | required |

## Workflow

### `batch`

Run several tools in order as ONE undo step. operations = [{"tool": name, "args": {...}}, ...]. Stops at the first error; with atomic = true the whole batch is undone then. Returns every result. render_preview and the file tools are not allowed inside.

| Parameter | Type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `atomic` | boolean |  |
| `operations` | list of object | required |

### `undo`

Undo the last change.

### `redo`

Redo.

## Prompts

Clients that list MCP prompts offer these as starting points.

- **`design_jersey`**: Design a complete team jersey from scratch. Arguments: `team` (required), `colors`, `number`, `player`, `sponsors`.
- **`review_design`**: Check the open design for problems and fix them. Arguments: none.

## Instructions the server sends to clients

> You are editing a sports jersey design in OpenJersey (a volleyball jersey designer). A design is one top and one bottom on one body (see get_overview, list_garments, set_garment) and a print sheet with all of their pieces laid out side by side. Objects (text, graphics, shapes, watermark patterns, logo placeholders, groups) sit on top of the pieces' base colours (set_piece_color). Units are millimetres on the sheet (x right, y down) unless you give a garment position: {"panel": "front"|"back", "across_mm": <from the centre line, positive = wearer's left>, "above_hem_mm": <height above the jersey hem>}. Workflow: call get_overview, then list_objects; make several related edits in one `batch` call (it undoes in one step); check the result with render_preview (use `piece` to zoom into one piece). Prefer editing existing objects over adding duplicates, keep sponsor placeholders where they are unless asked, and never overwrite files the user did not name.
